tn_muscle_block.blurb: A single sandstone boulder at the start of the Lilly Boulders field near Lancing, in the Obed and Clear Creek country. It sits on a side wall to your left as you enter the field, so it is the first stone most visitors meet. Ten problems cover a wide spread: several easy ones at V0 and V1, a handful in the middle, and two hard lines at V6 and V7. The surrounding hemlock-shaded field stays cooler than most Tennessee sandstone in summer, which makes this a decent warm-season stop. The short walk in and the mix of grades suit a casual session or a first look at the area.
tn_muscle_block.parking_note: Leave the car in the Lilly Overlook lot; the trailhead sign is at the far left side of it.
tn_muscle_block.approach: A short, easy trail drops about 0.2 miles from the lot, crosses the road, and joins a wooden walkway that leads straight into the boulder field. This block is the first one you reach.

tn_warm_up_wall_the.blurb: A long block in the Lilly Boulders field outside Lancing, set among hemlocks on sandstone. It has a low roof at one end and gently overhanging faces toward the other. Ten problems range from V0 up to V8, with the bulk in the easy to moderate bracket and a few much harder lines for people who want to push. As the name suggests, it works well early in a session. It is found by taking the first left fork off the approach trail and walking past the first boulder you meet, so it is close to the start of the field and quick to reach.
tn_warm_up_wall_the.parking_note: Park in the Lilly Overlook lot; the trailhead sign is at the far left of the lot.
tn_warm_up_wall_the.approach: Follow the short trail about 0.2 miles downhill, cross the road, and use the wooden walkway into the field. Take the first fork left and pass the first boulder; the wall is just beyond.

tn_mystery_groove_boulder.blurb: One of the boulders in the Front Area of Stone Fort, the well known bouldering field in the woods beside a golf course near Chattanooga. It lies in the first cluster of stones you meet on the way down from the parking area. About ten problems are listed here, running from very easy up to V6, with a few in the low-to-moderate range and the boulder's best known line around V4. Several faces and a back side offer different angles, so a group of mixed ability can all find something. Expect a busy, popular part of the field.

tn_the_bowling_ball.blurb: A boulder in the Front Area of Stone Fort, the wooded bouldering field near Chattanooga, close to where the climber path from the parking area enters the field. It sits beside another named block and has a Kingpin problem on its back. About ten problems are listed, and most are easy, in the V0 to V1 range, with a couple near V2 and V3 and two much harder lines around V6. That makes it a friendly spot to warm up or to bring someone newer to bouldering, with a few problems for stronger climbers on the same stone.
